messages:
Maya Patel: Quick sync 3: we need a firm decision on chat-completions payload shape for the Q2 roadmap. There's a growing customer ask for both `messages` (roles) and a compact `prompt_text` mode. Which way do we go?
Sam Lee: Launch goals: backward compatibility, streaming parity, function-calling parity, straightforward SDK migration, and no extra telemetry leakage. Also want perf within ~1.2x baseline.
Oliver Chen: Runtime reality: our serving stacks are tuned around `messages` (role tokens + KV cache alignment). Accepting freeform `prompt_text` means we must parse and normalize it server-side which adds CPU + memory churn. Naive support could add ~10-20% latency.
Jia Nguyen: For function calls & structured outputs we rely on deterministic role boundaries. If we admit `prompt_text` we need a canonicalizer that maps it to a messages array (system/user/assistant). Also need an option to reject ambiguous prompts.
Nina Torres: Enterprise asks: a minimal prompt option is attractive to reduce token count, but compliance teams want deterministic enforcement of system instructions and auditable transformations. That points to opt-in at the Dedicated/Private tier.
Sam Lee: Draft option: Hybrid endpoint that accepts either `messages` OR `prompt_text` (server rejects requests that send both). Server immediately canonicalizes to internal `messages[]` for execution. SDKs will emit deprecation/migration helpers. Host `messages` first for full feature parity; `prompt_text` as opt-in fallback.
Oliver Chen: Implementation plan: add canonicalization stage in API gateway, then route to two execution paths: fast-path for normalized `messages` and fallback-path for normalized `prompt_text`. We'll maintain the same streaming protocol but fallback path may require an initial parse pass before streaming tokens.
Jia Nguyen: Edge cases to handle: embedded role markers inside prompts (e.g., "Human:", "Assistant:"), multi-user transcripts, and prompts that mix system directives mid-turn. We'll build a regex-based heuristic plus a `strictParsing` flag that can be enabled per-tenant.
Maya Patel: Can we deliver streaming + function-calling parity day-one for hosted? If not, we need explicit feature gating so customers know which combos are supported.
Oliver Chen: Feasibility: streaming + functions are solid for native `messages`. For `prompt_text`, streaming is feasible but function-calling requires full canonicalization and signature extraction, so it should be gated. Recommend staged rollout: (1) messages -> streaming + functions, (2) prompt_text -> streaming only, (3) prompt_text + functions after canonicalizer accuracy improves.
Sam Lee: Proposed launch gates: (A) canonicalizer >=95% accuracy on our prompt test corpus, (B) streaming parity for `messages`, (C) SDK migration helpers cover >=80% of observed usage patterns, (D) telemetry tag `api.payload_variant` emitted for every request, and (E) enterprise opt-in path documented. Also need migration docs & customer comms.
Nina Torres: For Enterprise pilot: make `prompt_text` opt-in and limited to Dedicated/Private so clients can inspect transformation logs and tune `strictParsing`. We'll gather sample prompts from 3 pilot customers to refine heuristics.
Maya Patel: Owners & timeline: Maya+Sam write spec + payload examples; Oliver executes canonicalizer + router changes; Jia owns sanitizer + function-calling tests; Nina runs enterprise pilot. Deadlines?
Oliver Chen: Rough estimates: canonicalizer + unit tests 2 weeks, router + fast-path + perf tuning 3 weeks, SDK updates + docs 1 week. End-to-end canary ~6 weeks.
Sam Lee: Action items: Maya to post spec by Friday (include sample before/after normalizations), Oliver to set up perf benchmarks and results dashboard, Jia to produce function-call test corpus, Nina to recruit pilot customers and collect prompt samples.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary env created: `chat-hybrid-canary`. Reminder: tag relevant issues with #hybrid-chat and run canary load tests.
Maya Patel: Thanks team 3: I'll post the spec link when ready and ping infra for initial runs. :thumbsup:

---
Example normalization snippet for the spec (include as illustrative JSON in the doc):

```json
{
  "input_prompt": "System: You are a concise assistant. User: Summarize the plan.",
  "normalized_messages": [
    { "role": "system", "content": "You are a concise assistant." },
    { "role": "user", "content": "Summarize the plan." }
  ]
}
```

Note: server will emit `api.payload_variant` with values `messages` or `prompt_text` in telemetry and this should be surfaced in billing/monitoring so we can compare unit economics and error rates across variants.
